tools.description: forward a port of this sandbox to the user's machine, so a server started with the job tool can be opened in their browser
tools.name: forward

job_name.description: an optional associated job name; 1–10 characters from [a-z0-9-] (for add)

port.description: the TCP port inside the sandbox (for add and remove)

tools.description: run a shell command in the background. For a server, bind a fixed port and pass it as `port`; the tool forwards that same number, reports the URL the user opens it at, and does not discover an ephemeral port. You are told when it ends, and woken if you have ended your turn, so end your turn rather than waiting or polling for it.
tools.name: job

command.description: the command line (for action 'start'); if omitted, re-runs previous job by name

intent.description: for action 'start', what you are doing, as a 5 to 7 word phrase opening with a capitalised -ing verb, such as "Regenerating every golden in the scratch copy"

name.description: the job name; for start, use one short role such as 'check', not a specific compound such as 'cachecheck'—a live duplicate is automatically numbered, such as 'check-1'; 1–10 characters from [a-z0-9-] (for all actions except 'list', 'prune')

port.description: an optional TCP port inside the sandbox to forward to the user (for start)

respawn.description: for action 'start', start the command again each time it exits, still notifying you; stop the job to end it. Respawning gives up after 3 runs in a row each end within 2s
